steps: This video shows why structured output drifts in long conversations, and how to fix it. In turns one to five, TicketFlow sends each ticket with the J S O N schema, and Claude returns valid J S O N.
Then tool outputs pile up in the context window. By turn fifteen, more than twenty of them sit between the schema and the newest request, burying it.
On turn fifteen, Claude's J S O N comes back missing the priority field. This is format drift: the schema is still there, but it has lost attention under all those outputs.
A junior developer suggests lowering the temperature. That is not the fix. Temperature tunes how random the output is, not how much attention Claude pays to the schema.
So you add a validator. Every output is checked against the schema on every turn, and the turn fifteen J S O N is rejected for the missing priority field.
Then you clean the context. You prune stale outputs from early turns, summarize the rest into short notes like three A P I calls succeeded, and repeat the schema.

On the next turn the schema is back in focus. Claude returns valid J S O N and the check passes. The takeaway: validate every turn and keep long contexts lean. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
